Sts. Boris and Gleb

Saints

Sts. Boris and Gleb

Sts. Romanus and David · Sts. Holy Passion-bearers Boris and Gleb

Period
Killed 1015
Region
Rus
Titles / vocation
Martyr · Royal
Commemoration
July 24

Introduction

Sts. Boris and Gleb, the baptized princes Sts. Romanus and David, are remembered as passion-bearers in the Orthodox tradition of Rus.

Read the published life [1]

BackgroundLife and notable eventsDeath and martyrdomWritings and legacyChronology
Death / martyrdom

Murdered in 1015; their distinct attacks are described in the Orthodox life.

Read circumstances and sources

Background

The OCA identifies them as sons of Vladimir and places their deaths in the struggle following their father’s death.

[1] Official Orthodox hagiographic account · Published biographical account,paragraph 1; Published biographical account,paragraph 2; Published biographical account,paragraph 3

Life and notable events

Its narrative describes Boris refusing to seize power against his brother, and both princes becoming targets of Sviatopolk’s assassins.

[1] Official Orthodox hagiographic account · Published biographical account,paragraph 1; Published biographical account,paragraph 2; Published biographical account,paragraph 3

Death and martyrdom

Boris is attacked with lances and finally swords; Gleb is killed by his cook with a knife. The life dates the deaths to 1015.

[1] Official Orthodox hagiographic account · Published biographical account,paragraph 4; Published biographical account,paragraph 6; Published biographical account,paragraph 8

Writings and legacy

The account explains passion-bearing through their refusal to answer violence with violence. Mouravieff’s historical narrative below records their early veneration.

[1] Official Orthodox hagiographic account · Published biographical account,paragraph 7; Published biographical account,paragraph 8 · [2] Historical Church history · ChapterII,pp19–20,early veneration of Sts. Boris and Gleb,paragraph 1

The untimely end of the young princes, who tenderly loved each other, is described in an affecting manner by Nestor. The murderous sword cut them off both together while in the act of prayer : both together as pure sacrifices, sprinkled with their own innocent blood, they presented themselves before the Lord; and the Church being assured of their sanctity by the incorruption of their virgin bodies and by many signs of healing, soon began to ask their assistance in her prayers.

A nineteenth-century historical retelling attributed to Mouravieff. Its condensed collective wording does not replace the separately described attacks in the Orthodox life.

[2] Historical Church history · ChapterII, Further Establishment of the Faith, opening account of Sts. Boris and Gleb, pp19–20

Ye have heard that it hath been said, An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth:

But I say unto you, That ye resist not evil: but whosoever shall smite thee on thy right cheek, turn to him the other also.

And if any man will sue thee at the law, and take away thy coat, let him have thy cloke also.

And whosoever shall compel thee to go a mile, go with him twain.

Give to him that asketh thee, and from him that would borrow of thee turn not thou away.

Ye have heard that it hath been said, Thou shalt love thy neighbour, and hate thine enemy.

But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you;

That ye may be the children of your Father which is in heaven: for he maketh his sun to rise on the evil and on the good, and sendeth rain on the just and on the unjust.

For if ye love them which love you, what reward have ye? do not even the publicans the same?

And if ye salute your brethren only, what do ye more than others? do not even the publicans so?

Be ye therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect.

Related Scripture; not a claim that this passage narrates the saint’s life or is a prescribed feast-day reading.

[3] Public-domain Bible translation · Matthew 5: 38–48

Chronology

    A dynastic struggle threatens the brothers.

    [1] Official Orthodox hagiographic account · Published biographical account,paragraph 1; Published biographical account,paragraph 6

  2. 1015

    Sts. Boris and Gleb are killed.

    [1] Official Orthodox hagiographic account · Published biographical account,paragraph 1; Published biographical account,paragraph 5; Published biographical account,paragraph 8

  3. Later veneration

    The Church remembers them as passion-bearers.

    [1] Official Orthodox hagiographic account · Published biographical account,paragraph 7; Published biographical account,paragraph 8
